name: Ortur LM2 S2 10W
tagline: 10W Ortur LM2 S2: faster engraves than 5W on the same frame
tldr: Ortur LM2 S2 10W is the higher-power SKU in the LM2 S2 family: better cutting on thin wood and quicker fills than 5W, still open-frame and budget-oriented.
mainObjective: High-quality hobby and light-business engraving with light, slow cutting

engraveExample.description: Filled photo or logo on birch plywood

cutExample.description: Simple square cut-out from 3 mm basswood

pros: Cuts 3 mm basswood squares in ~6–10 min in our benchmarks
Filled engraving at ~60–150 mm/s: a 10 × 10 cm photo in ~12–18 min
Same frame and accessories as the lower-power LM2 S2
cons: Ortur's LU2-10A listing was out of stock in October 2026
Slightly wider ~0.08 mm spot: small text is a little less crisp than with the lower-power module
Stock thicker than 5 mm needs multiple passes and air assist
beginnerNotes: This profile is the 10W SKU on Ortur LM2 S2. Read the TL;DR and benchmarks above, then compare other power options via the chips before buying.
proTips: Run material test grids at engraving speeds first. Add air assist for light cuts. If cut jobs exceed ~30% of your week, open the higher-watt profile on this site and compare times.

editorialDepth.advantages: Ortur LM2 S2 10W suits makers who sell marks, photos, and gifts more than daily panel cutting. Reasonable open-frame entry price.
editorialDepth.limitations: Skip if you already quote 4 mm+ cutting in production. Not for cast acrylic or bare metal without spray.

faq.question: Is the LM2 S2 10W still available new?
faq.answer: Ortur's store listed the LM2 S2 with the LU2-10A 10W module at $209.99 in October 2026, but out of stock. Expect to buy it used or from remaining reseller stock; Ortur also runs pre-owned listings for its older machines.

faq.question: How thick can the LM2 S2 10W cut?
faq.answer: Ortur's page shows 12 mm wood and 5 mm acrylic cut in one pass, but those images sit in the LM2 Pro S2 section and may not apply to this frame. In our benchmarks a 10 × 10 cm square in 3 mm basswood takes about 6–10 min at 4–10 mm/s; plan 3–5 mm in one or two passes.

faq.question: Is the 10W worth it over the LM2 S2 5W?
faq.answer: For about $70 more on our tracked listings, yes in most cases: 3 mm cut times drop from 9–15 min to 6–10 min, and photo fills run at about 60–150 mm/s instead of 16–42 mm/s. The 5W only makes sense for engraving-only use on the smallest budget.

standoutFeatures.title: Big step for a small price gap
standoutFeatures.body: Roughly a third faster on 3 mm cuts and several times faster on fills than the lower-power LM2 S2, for about $70 more.

standoutFeatures.title: Good used value
standoutFeatures.body: Out of stock new in October 2026, it often shows up second-hand at entry-level prices with a large 400 × 400 mm frame.
